regulator: Food and Drugs Authority (FDA Ghana) – https://fdaghana.gov.gh

facts.title: Regulator and legal basis
facts.body: The FDA registers medicines under the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851), Part 7. No medicine may be imported, advertised or sold unless registered. The FDA reached WHO Maturity Level 3. Dossiers follow the ICH Common Technical Document (M4); submission is on paper or electronic files, not yet eCTD, and applicants check status with the FDA directly. The public product registry (verifypermit.fdaghana.gov.gh) lists every registered product with its holder, manufacturer, strength, form and expiry.

facts.title: A Ghanaian local agent holds the application
facts.body: A foreign manufacturer applies through a local representative or agent in Ghana (a licensed importer or wholesaler), named on the registration and on the public registry. The agent handles the application, the samples, variations and renewals.

facts.title: Six months target, about 70 days median
facts.body: The FDA decides a new application within six months when no query is raised, a fast-track application in 180 days and a reliance or renewal application in 90 days; queries get 12, then 6, then 3 months to answer. A 2024 review of African regulators measured the FDA's median approval time at about 70 calendar days, the shortest of those compared.

facts.title: Fees: USD 240 a year for an imported medicine (2023 schedule)
facts.body: The Fees and Charges (Miscellaneous Provisions) Regulations, 2023 (L.I. 2481) set the registration and re-registration fee for an imported allopathic medicine at the cedi equivalent of USD 240 per annum; a new chemical entity or a biological pays USD 360, an orphan drug USD 60. Variations for foreign products cost USD 500 (major) and USD 300 (minor); label evaluation USD 100 per product and variant; laboratory sample USD 200. Before 2023 (L.I. 2228 of 2016) an imported product paid USD 3,600 for a three-year registration, the 'USD 1,200 a year' still quoted by service providers. An FDA import levy of 1.80% of CIF value applies to drugs.

facts.title: Registration runs about three years, renewed through the agent
facts.body: Registrations on the public registry carry expiry dates about three years after approval and are renewed by the local agent; the registry flags products within three months of expiry. The FDA publishes recalls and alerts on unregistered products.

facts.title: Plant GMP approval before the dossier
facts.body: The manufacturing site needs FDA GMP approval before the product dossier is filed: an on-site audit (about three months the first time, two for renewal, USD 10,500) or a waiver when the site holds a valid GMP certificate from a stringent regulator listed by the FDA. Site approval is valid five years. Samples are tested in the FDA laboratory (USD 200 per sample).

facts.title: Duty and VAT
facts.body: Registered pharmaceuticals and their active ingredients are exempt from VAT (VAT Regulations as amended in 2024) and most finished medicines enter duty-free under the ECOWAS tariff; the FDA import levy of 1.80% of CIF applies. Importers must be licensed by the FDA (list published).

facts.title: Essential list 2017, NHIS reimbursement
facts.body: The Essential Medicines List (7th edition, 2017) sets levels of care A to D and marks medicines reimbursed by the National Health Insurance Scheme. Public procurement runs through the Ministry's and regional medical stores.

routes.label: Full review (FDA Ghana)
routes.description: CTD through a Ghanaian local agent after FDA GMP approval of the site (audit USD 10,500 or a stringent-regulator waiver), samples to the FDA laboratory. Six-month target; median about 70 days in 2024 reviews. USD 240 a year for an imported medicine under the 2023 fee schedule (USD 360 for a new chemical entity or biological), so about USD 720 over a three-year registration.

routes.label: Reliance / fast-track
routes.description: For products approved by a stringent regulator or WHO prequalified: reliance review with a 90-day target; fast-track for priorities in 180 days. Same fee: USD 240 a year (USD 360 for a new chemical entity).
